name: MTEB: Massive Text Embedding Benchmark
description: MTEB is a benchmark for text embeddings spanning 8 embedding tasks covering a total of 58 datasets and 112 languages. Tasks include bitext mining, classification, clustering, pair classification, reranking, retrieval, semantic textual similarity (STS), and summarization. The benchmark enables comprehensive evaluation of text embedding models and comes with open-source code and a public leaderboard.
creator: Niklas Muennighoff, Nouamane Tazi, Loïc Magne, Nils Reimers (Hugging Face, cohere.ai)
citeAs: Muennighoff, N., Tazi, N., Magne, L., & Reimers, N. (2023). MTEB: Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. arXiv:2210.07316v3 [cs.CL].
rai:dataCollection: Datasets were collected from a variety of existing sources including public APIs (arXiv, bioRxiv/medRxiv), Reddit posts, StackExchange posts, Amazon reviews, Twitter, Kaggle competitions, and existing NLP benchmarks (BEIR, SemEval, etc.). Some datasets (ArxivClustering, BiorxivClustering, MedrxivClustering, RedditClusteringP2P, StackExchangeClusteringP2P) were custom-made for MTEB using public APIs.
rai:dataCollectionType: Web API, Secondary Data analysis, Web Scraping, User-generated content data
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Data sources include: arXiv public API, bioRxiv/medRxiv API, Reddit posts, StackExchange posts, Amazon customer reviews, Twitter messages, Kaggle competition datasets, SemEval datasets (STS11-STS22), BEIR benchmark datasets, and other existing NLP datasets such as Banking77, Emotion, IMDB, MASSIVE, MTOP, BIOSSES, SICK-R, SummEval, BUCC, and Tatoeba.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For ArxivClustering P2P datasets, abstracts are concatenated to the title. For S2S datasets, only the title is used. For arXiv, only the first category is used when multiple categories are assigned. Subsets of labels are selected and articles sampled to yield splits with varying amounts and sizes of clusters.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Datasets are grouped into three categories based on text length: Sentence to sentence (S2S), Paragraph to paragraph (P2P), and Sentence to paragraph (S2P). For classification tasks, a logistic regression classifier with 100 maximum iterations is trained on train set embeddings. For clustering, a mini-batch k-means model with batch size 32 is used. Models are evaluated on test splits for all datasets except MSMARCO, where the dev split is used.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Cluster labels for ArxivClustering, BiorxivClustering, and MedrxivClustering are generated using categories given to papers by humans. For bioRxiv and medRxiv, the category is unique per paper. For arXiv, multiple categories can be assigned but only the first is used. Bitext mining datasets (BUCC, Tatoeba) use annotated translation pairs. Classification datasets use human-assigned labels (e.g., intents, sentiments, toxicity). STS datasets use continuous similarity scores from human annotators.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Mini-batch k-means (scikit-learn) for clustering evaluation; logistic regression (scikit-learn) for classification evaluation; cosine similarity for retrieval, STS, bitext mining, reranking, and summarization evaluation.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: MTEB uses versioning at both dataset and software levels to ensure reproducibility. JSON result files are made available on the Hugging Face Hub. The benchmark is open-source and community contributions of new datasets, tasks, or metrics are welcomed via pull requests. A public leaderboard is maintained at https://huggingface.co/spaces/mteb/leaderboard.
rai:dataSocialImpact: MTEB aims to simplify the selection of text embedding models for practitioners and researchers, reducing the 'blind' application of models to new use cases. By providing a comprehensive benchmark, it helps identify the strengths and weaknesses of individual models across diverse tasks and languages, potentially improving NLP applications in industry and research.
rai:dataBiases: MTEB average scores are biased towards tasks with many datasets, notably retrieval, classification, and clustering, due to task imbalance. Some models may have data contamination issues where parts of MTEB datasets overlap with model training data (e.g., SciDocsRR and MPNet/MiniLM training data). The benchmark does not control for such overlap.
rai:dataLimitations: 1. Long document datasets are missing; the longest datasets have a few hundred words. 2. Task imbalance exists, with summarization consisting of only a single dataset. 3. Retrieval and clustering tasks are English-only; multilingual coverage is limited to classification, STS, and bitext mining. 4. No code datasets are included. 5. Only natural language applications are covered; other modalities (e.g., images) are not benchmarked.
rai:dataUseCases: MTEB is designed for benchmarking and evaluating text embedding models across 8 tasks: bitext mining, classification, clustering, pair classification, reranking, retrieval, semantic textual similarity (STS), and summarization. It can be used for model selection, comparison of embedding approaches, and as a foundation for future embedding research. Datasets and results are available for use in training, testing, and validation contexts.
